markdown_content: ## Overview of Display Settings and Toggle Menu in Clo 2025.0 This section explains how Clo 2025.0 saves and applies display settings through the toggle menu embedded within project files. It details how these settings influence the workspace appearance when opening or importing project files, and how users can customize these settings for different workflow stages. ## How Display Settings Are Saved and Applied When you drag and drop a project file into an empty Clo workspace, the software automatically opens the file with the display settings (toggle menu configuration) saved within that project file. This means the workspace, including toggled options like quality render, schematic render, garment display elements, avatar visibility, and fabric texture, will appear exactly as saved. If you drop a project file into a workspace that already contains content, a pop-up window appears allowing you to decide whether to apply the display settings saved in the project file. This is controlled by a checkbox labeled **Display Settings**: - **Checked:** The project file’s saved display settings are applied, changing the toggle menu and view options accordingly. - **Unchecked:** The default display settings are applied instead, overriding the saved settings in the project file. This toggle menu control lets users decide between preserving the project's customized visual setup or using the default Clo display preferences. ## Default Display Settings in Clo 2025.0 The default display settings consist of specific toggle options preset by Clo 2025.0: - **Quality Render:** Off - **Schematic Render:** Off - **Garment Display:** Most options enabled except: - Show 2D Measurements: Off - Show Garment Fittings: Off - **Trim Display:** All options enabled - **Avatar Display:** Show Avatar and Show 3D Pen Avatar enabled - **Fabric Display:** Textured Surface enabled (not thick textured surface) - **Fit Maps:** Off - **Environment:** Show 3D Ground Shadow and Show 3D enabled These defaults provide a consistent baseline view when no custom display settings are applied. ## Practical Workflow Applications of Display Settings Display settings saved with project files can optimize workflows by tailoring the visual environment for different tasks or recipients: - **Sketching or Fitting Preparation:** Enable schematic views and strain/stress maps, disable avatar visibility to focus on the garment, hide confusing lines and pins, and show 2D measurements. - **Collaboration Between Brands and Vendors:** Vendors can receive stage-specific project files with toggles set to show all pins and strain maps in early stages for review, then switch to quality renders and hide avatars in final stages. - **Quality Control and Rendering:** Set display toggles to ensure quality renders are on and schematics are off before exporting or delivering files. Saving these toggle configurations within the project file ensures consistent viewing across different users and project stages, supporting standardized quality and communication. ## Important Limitations and Compatibility Notes - The toggle menu and display settings saving feature only works with project files saved in Clo version 2025.0 or later. - Older project files created before Clo 2025.0 will not contain saved toggle menu states. To use this feature, open older files in Clo 2025.0 and save them again, which embeds the toggle settings. - When importing files saved in Clo 2025.0 or later, users must manually decide whether to apply saved display settings or default settings via the pop-up checkbox. - This feature is designed to facilitate evolving project workflows and collaboration, allowing users to maintain visual consistency and quality standards throughout the design and review process. --- This document captures the functionality, default behaviors, use cases, and constraints of the Save Display Settings toggle menu feature introduced in Clo 2025.0, providing a detailed reference for users and developers implementing or utilizing this capability.
